ns2:section.sectionText: Behavioral Seminar in Consumer Psychology. Restricted to Ph.D. students in Business Administration, Accountancy, and Psychology. This course is the first half of a two-semester sequence on consumer information processing. (The second half will be offered in fall 2010.) This semester will review representative general theories of information processing, followed by a discussion of theory and research on the various stages of processing that occur en route to a consumer judgment or decision, including: knowledge accessibility, attention and comprehension, the representation of information in memory, retrieval, inference and integration, the translation of subjective inferences into an overt response, and decision processes. (The second half covers special topics, including motivation, affect, attitude formation and change, communication and persuasion, and cultural influences on judgment.) The format will be lecture and discussion.
